faq: Can you audit without my code?
Yes. Basic and Standard work from an installable build, such as a Play testing link or an APK. Premium includes a code review and needs read-only repository access.
Will you fix what you find?
The audit gives you the list and the plan. Fixes can be ordered through our Android feature work or maintenance services, and Premium includes priced options so you can choose.
Do you check Play policy risks?
We check against Google Play's published policies, covering permissions, data safety, billing, ads and metadata. Google decides on every app, so we flag likely problems rather than promise approval.
Can you audit an unreleased app?
Yes. Send an internal testing link or an APK and we review it the same way. Early reviews let you fix problems before testers or Google see them.
desc:
An Android app audit from Ecom Swift LLC is a written, prioritized inspection of your app: crashes, slow screens, battery use, accessibility and Google Play policy risks, each with a clear fix. You learn what to repair first and what can wait.

## What is an Android app audit?

An Android app audit is a structured inspection of a live or unreleased app that ends in a ranked list of problems and recommended fixes. We install the app on phones of different sizes and use it the way a new customer would. If you share your code, we read the key modules too.

The result is a document you can hand to any developer, or back to us, and act on straight away. It replaces guessing with evidence.

## Why problems hide inside Android apps

Android runs on thousands of device models, several operating system versions and many screen sizes. An app that works on the phone it was built on can still crash on a budget handset, stretch badly on a tablet or drain the battery overnight. Most owners only find out through angry store comments or a sudden rise in uninstalls.

Google Play adds another layer. Policies on permissions, data safety, subscriptions and target API level change, and an app that ignored them can lose visibility or have an update rejected. A planned inspection finds these risks before your users or the store do.

## How an audit improves retention and quality

People delete apps that feel slow, confusing or unreliable, and they rarely explain why. An audit connects the symptoms to causes. A slow cold start might come from heavy work on the main thread. A drop-off after sign-in might come from a screen that asks for too much at once. A crash on older phones might trace to one library call.

Because every issue is ranked by impact and effort, your budget goes to the fixes that matter. You avoid rebuilding what works and you stop polishing screens that nobody reaches.

## What a strong Android audit covers

- Installation and first launch on a small phone and a large phone.
- Walkthrough of the main user flows, from sign-up to the core action.
- Crash, freeze and error behavior, including what happens with no network.
- Cold start time, scrolling smoothness and memory use.
- Battery drain from background work, location use and wake locks.
- Accessibility basics: text scaling, contrast, touch target size and screen reader labels.
- Google Play policy checks: permissions, data safety form, ads and subscription wording.
- Code structure, dependency age and obvious security gaps when code is shared.
- A ranked issue list with the reason each issue matters and the estimated effort.

## How we run the audit

We start by agreeing what the app should do and who uses it. Then we test on real devices and emulators, record each issue with steps to reproduce it and sort them into urgent, important and nice to have. The Basic package covers the main flows and top issues. Standard goes deeper into speed, battery, accessibility and policy, and includes a walkthrough call. Premium adds code reading, a security and data checklist and a fix plan with options you can choose from.

We never change your app during the audit. If you want the fixes done, we quote them separately from the list.

## Do this, avoid that: getting value from an audit

**Do:**
- Tell us which flows earn you money or keep users coming back.
- Share crash reports and Play Console warnings if you have them.
- Send a test account that covers every user role.
- Mention devices where users already complain.
- Read the top of the list first, then decide the order of work.

**Avoid:**
- Fixing visual details while a crash remains open.
- Hiding known problems, which only slows the audit.
- Treating the report as a one-time document that never gets revisited.
- Ignoring policy warnings because the app still works today.
- Starting a rewrite before you know which parts are sound.

## Who benefits from an audit

A founder who bought or inherited an app from another developer can learn what condition it is really in. A business owner whose ratings are falling can find the cause behind the complaints. A team about to add features or hire developers can check the foundation before building on it. The audit also suits owners of an unreleased app who want a second opinion before launch.

## What we need from you

Send the app name, a Play testing link or an APK, and a test login. Code access is optional and is given through your repository as a collaborator or read-only team member. We never need your passwords, and we never ask for your Google account sign-in. A short note about your goals and worries helps us aim the audit at what matters to you.
